rationale: Bought a mature relational/analytic database (ASE, IQ) plus mobile middleware to compete with Oracle in the data tier.
outcome: Closed July 2010; Sybase ASE and IQ sat in SAP's database portfolio alongside HANA.

rationale: Storage leader moved up-stack into MPP analytic databases under a big-data banner.
outcome: Terms never disclosed (one analyst guessed $300-400M); Greenplum was folded into the Pivotal spinout in 2013 and open-sourced in 2015.

rationale: Added a data-warehouse appliance to IBM's analytics push; Netezza already built on IBM hardware.
outcome: Closed late 2010; product rebranded PureData System for Analytics and later revived as Netezza Performance Server.

rationale: Gave HP a columnar analytic database after it phased out its Neoview warehouse.
outcome: Vertica moved to HPE in 2015 and then to Micro Focus in the 2017 HPE software spin-merge.

rationale: Bought the 89% it did not own to add MapReduce-style analytics on parallel clusters to its warehouse.
outcome: Closed Q2 2011; Aster functions were later folded into Teradata's Vantage platform.

rationale: Bet on unstructured-data search and analytics software to pivot HP away from PCs.
outcome: HP took an $8.8B impairment in Nov 2012 alleging accounting improprieties, making it a byword for overpayment; offer was GBP 25.50/share (~GBP 7.1B fully diluted).

rationale: Added a columnar MPP analytic engine to Actian's database roll-up (Ingres, Versant, Pervasive).
outcome: Rebranded Actian Matrix; ParAccel code had earlier been licensed as the basis of Amazon Redshift.

rationale: Bought a CouchDB-based JSON database-as-a-service to compete with cloud-native DBaaS such as DynamoDB.
outcome: Became IBM Cloudant, a managed NoSQL service on IBM Cloud.

rationale: Bought a data-management platform for third-party audience data to power Oracle's marketing cloud.
outcome: Became core of Oracle Data Cloud; Oracle exited the advertising business in 2024.

rationale: Took in-house its main reseller of firehose social data to own the enterprise data-licensing business.
outcome: Closed May 2014; price disclosed later in a 10-Q ($107.3M cash plus stock).

rationale: Added open-core embedded reporting to TIBCO's Spotfire analytics line.
outcome: Became TIBCO Jaspersoft; TIBCO's 10-Q shows a total purchase price of about $188M.

rationale: Acqui-hired a SQL-on-Hadoop engineering team as Hadoop threatened the warehouse.
outcome: Asset deal (with Revelytix) folded into Teradata's Hadoop/unified data architecture work.

rationale: Bought a Hadoop consulting shop to sell services around open-source data lakes.
outcome: Became Teradata's Think Big consulting brand.

rationale: Take-private of a slowing integration/analytics vendor at $24/share incl. debt; Vista's largest deal to date.
outcome: Closed late 2014; TIBCO was later combined with Citrix under Vista/Elliott in 2022.

rationale: Bought a real-time backend-as-a-service to attract mobile developers to Google Cloud.
outcome: Grew into Google's main app-development platform, including the Firestore database.

rationale: Bought offline purchase data linked to digital audiences for its marketing data cloud.
outcome: WSJ reported price above $1.2B; asset ended up inside the advertising unit Oracle shut in 2024.

rationale: Bought the leading commercial R distribution to bring data-science tooling into SQL Server and Azure.
outcome: Became Microsoft R Server/Machine Learning Server, later retired.

rationale: Storage vendor bought an open-core ETL/BI suite it already OEM'd, framed around IoT analytics.
outcome: Pentaho kept its brand and was folded into Hitachi Vantara in 2017; an outside estimate put price at $500-600M.

rationale: Bought a hosted Elasticsearch provider to build a first-party managed service.
outcome: Found became Elastic Cloud, now Elastic's main growth engine.

rationale: Bought a distributed transactional key-value store for its own cloud services.
outcome: Downloads were pulled at the deal; Apple open-sourced FoundationDB in April 2018.

rationale: Take-private at $48.75/share after activist pressure, to retool the data-integration leader for subscription/cloud.
outcome: Closed Aug 2015; re-IPO'd in 2021 and agreed to be acquired by Salesforce in 2025.

rationale: Added on-premises mobile dashboards to complement cloud Power BI.
outcome: Tech folded into SQL Server Reporting Services mobile reports and Power BI.

rationale: Bought an open-source network-data shipper to seed a lightweight data-collection layer.
outcome: Became the template for Elastic's Beats family of data shippers.

rationale: Take-private of a BI vendor at $30.50/share (40% premium) amid activist pressure.
outcome: Closed Aug 2016; Qlik became a PE roll-up platform, buying Attunity (2019) and Talend (2023).

rationale: HR/finance SaaS vendor bought Hadoop-native analytics to add data prep and analysis.
outcome: Technology resurfaced as Workday Prism Analytics; standalone product was wound down.

rationale: Bought a Seattle ML-tooling startup (ex-GraphLab/Dato) for talent and on-device ML.
outcome: Team absorbed into Apple; Turi Create open-sourced in 2017.

rationale: Bought the largest data-science community (800k+ users) to feed Google Cloud's AI ecosystem.
outcome: Still runs as a distinct Kaggle brand within Google.

rationale: Added ad-verification and attention analytics to Oracle Data Cloud.
outcome: Price reported by Recode as above $850M; unit shut with Oracle's 2024 ad-business exit.

rationale: ERP vendor bought cloud-native BI to add analytics on top of its applications.
outcome: Run as Infor Birst, Infor's embedded BI layer.

rationale: Bought API-led integration to connect data across customers' systems into Salesforce clouds.
outcome: Closed May 2018; became Salesforce Integration Cloud and a building block for its data platform.

rationale: Bought marketing-data integration and analytics for Marketing Cloud.
outcome: Rebranded Marketing Cloud Intelligence; price reported (>$800M) by Calcalist.

rationale: All-stock merger of the two leading Hadoop distributors to end price competition; $5.2B is combined equity value.
outcome: Closed Jan 2019; growth stalled and Cloudera was taken private by KKR and CD&R in 2021.

rationale: Bought the largest third-party MongoDB-as-a-service host to move its users onto Atlas.
outcome: Closed by early 2019; mLab users were migrated to Atlas and mLab was retired.

rationale: Bought the open-source enterprise Linux/Kubernetes leader for hybrid cloud at $190/share.
outcome: Closed July 9, 2019; IBM's largest deal ever, Red Hat run as a distinct unit.

rationale: Bought self-service cloud ELT as a low-cost funnel for cloud data-warehouse customers.
outcome: Closed Nov 2018; Stitch survived Talend's 2021 Thoma Bravo buyout and 2023 sale to Qlik.

rationale: Bought the distributed-PostgreSQL extension to scale Postgres on Azure.
outcome: Became Hyperscale (Citus), later Azure Cosmos DB for PostgreSQL; extension stayed open source.

rationale: Bought data-pipeline tooling to ease migrations into BigQuery and Google Cloud.
outcome: Folded into Google Cloud migration tooling; Globes reported unconfirmed $100-150M.

rationale: BI vendor bought change-data-capture replication to move into data integration.
outcome: Closed May 2019; became Qlik Replicate/Qlik Data Integration.

rationale: Snowflake's first acquisition, a SQL query UI to improve its web interface.
outcome: Became the basis of the Snowsight interface.

rationale: Bought an open-source mobile database and sync service to extend Atlas to edge devices.
outcome: Closed May 2019; became Atlas Device Sync, which MongoDB deprecated in 2024.

rationale: Bought endpoint security to extend Elastic's search engine into a SIEM/security suite.
outcome: Closed 2019; became the endpoint layer of Elastic Security.

rationale: Bought a semantic-layer BI tool to sit on top of BigQuery and multi-cloud warehouses.
outcome: Closed Feb 2020 after UK CMA clearance; now Google Cloud's BI layer.

rationale: All-stock purchase of the BI leader to make analytics a core Salesforce cloud.
outcome: Closed Aug 2019; the largest data-tools deal of the decade.

rationale: Distressed asset buy of the third Hadoop distributor after it nearly shut down.
outcome: Became HPE Ezmeral Data Fabric.

rationale: Bought streaming metrics/APM for cloud-native observability; Splunk's largest deal then (60% cash/40% stock).
outcome: Became Splunk Observability Cloud; Splunk itself sold to Cisco in 2024.

rationale: Dell-family consolidation for Kubernetes; Pivotal also carried Greenplum and GemFire data products. $2.7B is enterprise value.
outcome: Closed Dec 2019; Greenplum moved into VMware Tanzu and then to Broadcom with VMware in 2023.

rationale: PE-backed data-quality roll-up added location intelligence and data enrichment.
outcome: Closed Dec 2019; combined company renamed Precisely in 2020.
